content.value_statement: Federal contracting research is fragmented across sources and often lacks clear evidence boundaries. This skill structures approved research, records sources, and produces traceable findings or validated briefs.
actual_capabilities: Presents a nine-option menu for opportunity, competitor, recompete, teaming, market, pricing, and research-refresh workflows.
Creates a source plan with sanitized parameters and requires explicit provider approval before public web research.
Uses approved installed capabilities for SAM.gov, USASpending, GSA CALC+, native web, and optional Tavily research.
Maintains evidence identifiers, source-call records, retrieval times, limitations, conflicts, inferences, and unresolved questions.
Builds and validates optional DOCX briefs from normalized research records with citation and numeric checks.
limitations: Live research depends on installed and authenticated MCP or web capabilities.
Public evidence alone cannot support a bid or no-bid recommendation.
The skill does not provide legal, cybersecurity, export-control, responsibility, or financial-health determinations.
DOCX generation requires Python, python-docx, and a compatible document renderer.

use_cases.title: Screen a Federal Opportunity
use_cases.description: Assess public requirements, deadlines, eligibility, and company fit while separating sourced facts from internal assumptions.

use_cases.title: Build a Recompete Pipeline
use_cases.description: Organize award end dates, modifications, incumbents, agency patterns, and vehicle constraints into a qualified monitoring pipeline.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Teaming Candidates
use_cases.description: Compare public registration, certifications, awards, customer overlap, and apparent role fit without overstating trust or responsibility.

prompt_templates.title: Find Relevant Opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me find federal opportunities for cybersecurity support in Virginia. Start with the workflow menu, then ask for the minimum search criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Screen a Solicitation
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this solicitation and my capability statement. Separate public evidence from company facts, identify missing bid inputs, and withhold a verdict when context is incomplete.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Recompete Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a recompete pipeline for civilian agency cloud services over the next 24 months. Track award identifiers, incumbents, end dates, modifications, and uncertainty.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Evidence Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Refresh the attached prior research using approved sources. Preserve earlier evidence, record changed assumptions, recompute numeric findings, and produce a validated DOCX brief.

output_examples.input: Find active help desk opportunities for an 8(a) firm in Maryland.
output: Opportunity candidates are listed with notice identifiers, agencies, response deadlines, set-asides, and source references.
Each candidate separates verified facts from inferred fit and notes missing attachments or date uncertainty.
No bid recommendation is made until company capabilities and risk tolerances are supplied.

output_examples.input: Analyze an incumbent for an upcoming recompete.
output: The incumbent profile distinguishes prime awards, subawards, obligations, ceiling values, and public claims.
Entity ambiguity and incomplete public records are stated as limitations.
Potential competitive implications are labeled as inferences with supporting evidence identifiers.

output_examples.input: Compare labor-rate context for senior cloud engineers.
output: Published ceiling rates are grouped by labor category, experience, education, geography, year, and contract source.
The assessment explains why ceiling rates are not paid rates, proposed rates, or an independent price-reasonableness decision.

best_practices: Provide exact notice, award, agency, entity, NAICS, PSC, and date details when available.
Review sanitized search terms and provider disclosures before approving any public research.
Supply internal capabilities, past performance, staffing, access, strategy, and risk tolerances before requesting a bid recommendation.
anti_patterns: Do not place proprietary, classified, privacy-sensitive, export-controlled, or source-selection content into public queries.
Do not treat search hits, active flags, award ceilings, or CALC+ rates as conclusive evidence.
Do not request unsupported legal, responsibility, financial-health, or guaranteed award conclusions.

faq.question: Which research workflows are supported?
faq.answer: The skill covers opportunity discovery, bid screening, competitor analysis, recompetes, teaming, agency markets, pricing context, and prior-research refreshes.

faq.question: Does the skill make bid decisions?
faq.answer: It can recommend a decision only when complete internal company context and stated tolerances are available. Public data alone is insufficient.

faq.question: Which sources can the skill use?
faq.answer: It can use approved installed SAM.gov, USASpending, GSA CALC+, native web, and Tavily capabilities according to the selected mode.

faq.question: Is web research automatic?
faq.answer: No. The skill presents sanitized terms, proposed URLs, provider choices, limits, and disclosures before requesting explicit approval.

faq.question: Can it create a report?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create an optional DOCX brief after validating the research record, citations, calculations, structure, and rendered pages.

faq.question: How does it handle sensitive documents?
faq.answer: Uploaded content remains untrusted internal evidence. The workflow prohibits sending document text or sensitive information to public providers.
